newsitem.title: USA: U.N. to recommend Iraq oil deal renewal at $2 bln.
newsitem.headline: U.N. to recommend Iraq oil deal renewal at $2 bln.

text.p: The United Nations will recommend renewal of Iraq's "oil-for-food" accord when the $2 billion deal comes up for Security Council review before the plan's expiration on June 7, a senior U.N. official said Wednesday.

A report by Secretary-General Kofi Annan to the Security Council, expected to be delivered before the current scheme expires, will cite the need to continue the humanitarian aid program for ordinary Iraqis despite some snags in delivering supplies during the first six months of operation, said the offical, who didn't want to be named.

"The U.N. is ready to recommend an extension. Most governments support a deal. Even the Americans have no problem, despite wanting some changes and additions (to the resolution)," said the official, who is involved in the administration of the scheme.

The "oil-for-food" accord, which went into effect on December 10, allows Iraq to sell up to $2 billion of crude oil over six months. Under the strictly-controlled deal, nearly two-thirds of oil receipts are earmarked for food and medicine purchases for Iraqis suffering under stringent U.N. sanctions since Baghdad's 1990 invasion of Kuwait.

The official said there was some discussion that Washington wanted to alter procedures for dealing with the northern Kurdish regions of Iraq, which is not under control of the central Baghdad government.
Without going into detail, the official said U.S. suggestions for changes were not supported by other council members and were believed to have been dropped by Washington.
"There are also calls to look at the needs of the south (southern parts of Iraq), since the north gets twice as much per capita than the south," noted the official.

The U.N. will not include a recommendation to raise oil sales above the current $2 billion ceiling, the official said. "Iraq wants an expansion in sales, but an expansion would be extremely difficult," said the U.N. official.
In recent days the U.S. has been cagey about its stance on renewal, with officials at the U.N. mission saying Washington has yet to make up its mind.

Even if approval is forthcoming before June 7, officials and diplomats were unclear whether there would be any gap between the last oil sales under the current scheme and the first under a new accord.
